key_insight: The paper makes RUDE constitutive models stable, thermodynamically admissible, and more interpretable by combining input compression, split networks, and a differentiable projection layer with a new compact "rheome" representation.
engineering_relevance: This enables data-driven rheology models that generalize better beyond training flows and are more suitable for CFD and process design of complex soft materials.
method: Log-compress input invariants to improve conditioning during training
Use a split-network architecture to reduce stiffness and improve learnability
Enforce the Clausius--Duhem inequality with a differentiable projection layer; summarize learned tensor-basis contributions with a rheome
evidence_signal: The framework was trained on LAOS data for both a synthetic multi-mode Giesekus model and an entangled silicone polymer melt, then tested successfully on unseen steady shear, transient stress growth, and extensional flows.
watch_item: The approach adds architectural and projection complexity, so enforcing thermodynamic constraints and preserving physical fidelity in new materials or CFD implementations may require careful tuning and validation.
paper_title: Stable and Interpretable Multi-Mode Rheological Universal Differential Equations (mmRUDEs) for Data-Driven Constitutive Modeling
